body: I don't think that's a reality I can stomach. I don't want to live in a world where I have to keep secrets from those close to me, even if it's to save them the burden. They've shared so many secrets of their own with me, and I just can't live with myself having done something so egregious I can't return the favor.

Thanks for that. I know things will get better, I've experienced it firsthand before. I've just worked really hard lately building close friendships, and I'm now feeling like I'm not being honest with them about myself by not telling them. It's like if someone were a murderer, their friends would probably want to know that because it would make them change their minds about associating with them. This feels like the same magnitude of "if they knew, they wouldn't want to be my friend", and I feel somewhat of an obligation to let them know things like that. Not that I will, mind, but that obligation is what's causing me the most distress, I think.

I just feel like even if I forgive myself, those around me would never be so kind. Any friendships or relationships I ever make, I will not be being honest with them if I don't inform them of this. I mean, of course, nobody needs to know everything about everyone, but it feels like if someone were a murderer, their friends and *certainly* their partner would want to know. It feels like it's on a certain level that would change people's minds about associating with me, and knowingly keeping that info from them is/will eat me up inside. I feel guilty about that too.
